source_en: Home from the library reading room.
Resident, back from the university.
Bringing my notes home. Two notebooks.
Checking water rations at home.
Logged campus changes. Going home.
Bringing water to Mother and sister.
Counted lecture hall cracks. Going home.
Home to my mother and sister.
Taking home six notebooks now.
Home from my polytechnic engineering lab.
Home to my husband. He hates lateness.
Retiring from the tram depot.
Lost my papers. I never notice things.
Taking my son to the polyclinic.
Visiting my late mother's grave.
Teaching my political science seminar.
Nothing to note. I stopped noticing.
To the dormitory. Family's in Kutaisi.
The paint is peeling on your booth. Top left corner. Weeks now.
Is the air always this thick? It feels… heavy today.
I saw a tree turn gray while I was walking. Quite pretty.
The static on the TV… if you stare, it looks like snow.
I’m going to watch the sunset. I think it’s the last one.
Do you feel the world getting thinner? I can see right through it.
Thanks. You should probably fix that light soon.
Try not to look at the sky for too long.
Enjoy the view, officer. It’s quite a show.
This is a mistake. I have notes. I can prove it.
Fine. In here I can keep counting without any interruption.
The pattern… there was a pattern… I almost had it…
Wait… mommy! I was so close to figuring it out…
Where are you coming from?
The library. Closed at seven. Their clock runs two minutes slow.
Campus. Almost empty. I log what changed since yesterday. Then water.
The old lecture halls. Third row. I counted forty-one cracks.
The medical institute. Second-year anatomy. Demanding, but I like precision.
The bread queue, then home. I live alone now. Quieter for notes.
The university. Full lecture schedule today. Everyone came back.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
Tired. Late hours with my notes. Stress, not a symptom. I checked.
Hair in the brush every morning. Thirty-two strands today. I count.
I bruise at a touch. The numbers keep going when eyes close.
Nothing. I sleep ten hours a night and barely notice anything.
Nothing. I am twenty-three, officer. My body recovers fast.
Fine. I burned the notebooks. Stopped counting things. I feel much better.
The paint on your booth is peeling, top left. Wrong for weeks.
Your light flickers on a three-second interval. Has it always?
Thirty percent fewer people through here than last week. I counted.
The intervals are getting shorter. Something is accelerating. I have data.
The patterns are converging. I thought finding them would be a relief.
Six notebooks full. I do not know who they are for anymore.
